introduction: The git_server spec implements an internal git smart HTTP server for af-hub, exposing workspace repositories over HTTP at `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/` on the same port as the REST API. Note: requirements referencing go-git transport/server APIs are based on PRD descriptions and should be cross-checked against the installed go-git v5 library before implementation.

glossary.MountHandlers: The function convention used across af-hub specs to register HTTP route handlers on the Echo server instance.
glossary.PlainOpen: The go-git function `git.PlainOpen(path string)` that opens an existing git repository at the given filesystem path.
glossary.ReceivePackSession: A go-git server transport session that handles push protocol negotiation.
glossary.UploadPackSession: A go-git server transport session that handles fetch/clone protocol negotiation.
glossary.WORKSPACE_ROOT: The filesystem root directory under which all workspace local clones are stored, one subdirectory per workspace slug.
glossary.WWW-Authenticate: The HTTP response header sent with 401 responses to prompt git clients to supply Basic auth credentials.
glossary.af_admin_: The credential prefix identifying a hub admin token.
glossary.af_key_: The credential prefix identifying a hub API key.
glossary.af_pat_: The credential prefix identifying a hub Personal Access Token.
glossary.apikit: The `github.com/txsvc/apikit` foundation library providing auth middleware and permission registration for af-hub.
glossary.apikit.Permission: The type in apikit used to register named permission scopes for PATs.
glossary.clone_status: A field on the workspace database row tracking the state of the local git clone; valid values include 'ready', 'cloning', 'failed', and 'archived'.
glossary.git-receive-pack: The git service that handles push data transfer from client to server.
glossary.git-upload-pack: The git service that handles fetch and clone data transfer from server to client.
glossary.git:read: A PAT permission scope granting clone and fetch access to workspace repositories the PAT owner has access to.
glossary.git:write: A PAT permission scope granting push access to workspace repositories the PAT owner has access to, implying read access.
glossary.head_sha: A database column on the workspace row storing the SHA of the HEAD commit of the local clone.
glossary.info/refs: The git smart HTTP discovery endpoint that advertises available refs for a repository, parameterized by service name.
glossary.org-slug: The URL-safe identifier for an organization, used as the first path segment in git URLs.
glossary.org_id: The database foreign key on a workspace row referencing the organization that owns the workspace.
glossary.pkt-line: The git binary framing format used in the smart HTTP protocol to encode variable-length records in ref advertisements and pack negotiation.
glossary.server.Loader: The go-git interface `transport/server.Loader` that resolves a transport endpoint to a repository storer.
glossary.storer.Storer: The go-git interface representing a repository's storage backend, returned by the custom Loader.
glossary.transport.Endpoint: The go-git type representing a parsed git remote URL, used by the server transport to identify the target repository.
glossary.transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound: The go-git sentinel error returned by a Loader when the requested repository cannot be found or is not ready.
glossary.trunk: The subdirectory within a workspace's local clone directory that contains the bare or working git repository, at path `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<slug>/trunk/`.
glossary.workspace-slug: The URL-safe identifier for a workspace, used as the second path segment in git URLs.
glossary.workspaces:read: An existing PAT permission scope granting read access to the workspace REST API.
glossary.workspaces:write: An existing PAT permission scope granting write access to the workspace REST API.
glossary./git/:org/:slug.git/info/refs: Git smart HTTP ref advertisement endpoint; returns available refs for the given repository.
glossary./git/:org/:slug.git/git-upload-pack: Git smart HTTP endpoint that handles fetch/clone data transfer.
glossary./git/:org/:slug.git/git-receive-pack: Git smart HTTP endpoint that handles push data transfer.
glossary.service=git-upload-pack: Query parameter on info/refs GET requests requesting the upload-pack (fetch) ref advertisement.
glossary.service=git-receive-pack: Query parameter on info/refs GET requests requesting the receive-pack (push) ref advertisement.
glossary.service: The query parameter on info/refs GET requests specifying which git service to invoke (git-upload-pack or git-receive-pack).
glossary..git: The required suffix on git repository URLs in the path scheme (e.g. /git/org/repo.git).
glossary.Authorization: Basic: HTTP Basic authentication header format used by git clients to pass credentials (username:password base64-encoded).
glossary.Authorization: The HTTP header carrying authentication credentials (Basic or Bearer).
glossary.ready: The clone_status value indicating a workspace's local git clone is complete and the repository is available for git operations.
glossary.<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<slug>/trunk/: The filesystem path to a workspace's local git clone, composed of the workspace root, the workspace slug, and the trunk subdirectory.
glossary.:org: URL path parameter representing the organization slug in the git server URL scheme.
glossary.:slug: URL path parameter representing the workspace slug in the git server URL scheme.
glossary.Load(ep transport.Endpoint): The method on the server.Loader interface that resolves a transport.Endpoint to a storer.Storer for a git repository.
glossary.server.NewServer(loader): The go-git function that creates a transport.Transport implementing git server protocol logic using the given Loader.
glossary.AdvertisedReferences(): A method on go-git's Session interface that returns the set of refs (branches, tags) available in the repository.
glossary.WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=\"af-hub\": The HTTP response header sent with 401 to prompt git clients for Basic auth credentials.

user_story.goal: access workspace repositories using standard git commands over HTTP
user_story.benefit: I can clone, fetch, and push without depending on the upstream remote or leaving the platform

acceptance_criteria.action: register four routes on the Echo instance: GET `/git/:org/:slug.git/info/refs`, POST `/git/:org/:slug.git/git-upload-pack`, POST `/git/:org/:slug.git/git-receive-pack`, and a shared auth middleware applied to all four routes
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the HTTP server starts up via `MountHandlers`

acceptance_criteria.action: respond with the ref advertisement for fetch/clone using the git smart HTTP protocol
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type `application/x-git-upload-pack-advertisement` and a pkt-line encoded ref advertisement body
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request arrives at `/git/:org/:slug.git/info/refs` with `service=git-upload-pack`

acceptance_criteria.action: respond with the ref advertisement for push using the git smart HTTP protocol
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type `application/x-git-receive-pack-advertisement` and a pkt-line encoded ref advertisement body
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request arrives at `/git/:org/:slug.git/info/refs` with `service=git-receive-pack`

acceptance_criteria.action: stream the fetch/clone pack negotiation between the git client and the `UploadPackSession`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type `application/x-git-upload-pack-result` and a streaming pack response body

acceptance_criteria.action: stream the push pack data between the git client and the `ReceivePackSession`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type `application/x-git-receive-pack-result` and a streaming pack response body

edge_cases.action: reject the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a pkt-line error body per the git smart HTTP specification
edge_cases.error_condition: the `service` query parameter on `info/refs` is absent or is not `git-upload-pack` or `git-receive-pack`

edge_cases.action: not match any registered git route, falling through to the default 404 handler
edge_cases.error_condition: a request arrives at a git endpoint without the `.git` suffix in the path

requirements.title: HTTP Basic authentication for git clients

user_story.goal: authenticate to the git server using a hub credential as the HTTP Basic auth password
user_story.benefit: I can use standard git tooling and credential helpers without custom configuration

acceptance_criteria.action: resolve the credential to the associated user or admin identity and attach it to the request context; ignore the username field
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: passes the request to the next handler with the resolved identity in context
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a git request arrives with an `Authorization: Basic` header whose password field contains a valid hub credential (prefixed `af_key_`, `af_pat_`, or `af_admin_`)

acceptance_criteria.action: halt the request and return an authentication challenge
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 401 with header `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="af-hub"` and no body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a git request arrives with no `Authorization` header

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 401 with no `WWW-Authenticate` header
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a git request arrives with an `Authorization: Basic` header whose password does not match any known hub credential

edge_cases.action: reject the request as invalid credentials
edge_cases.error_condition: the `Authorization` header is present but malformed (not valid Base64 or missing the colon separator)

edge_cases.action: accept any non-empty string as the username field in HTTP Basic auth and use only the password field for credential resolution

requirements.title: Register git:read and git:write PAT permission scopes

user_story.goal: issue PATs with fine-grained git access scopes
user_story.benefit: agents and CI bots can be granted only the git permissions they need without broader workspace API access

acceptance_criteria.action: register `git:read` and `git:write` as named `apikit.Permission` scopes with apikit so they are available for PAT issuance and validation
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the git server module is initialized

acceptance_criteria.action: treat `git:write` as implying read access, so a PAT with only `git:write` may perform both fetch and push operations
keep `git:read` and `git:write` independent from `workspaces:read` and `workspaces:write`; a PAT may hold git scopes without workspace API scopes and vice versa

edge_cases.action: reject the push operation
edge_cases.error_condition: a PAT with `git:read` scope attempts a push (POST to `git-receive-pack`)

edge_cases.action: reject the request as unauthorized
edge_cases.error_condition: a PAT with neither `git:read` nor `git:write` scope attempts any git operation

user_story.goal: resolve the correct workspace repository from the request URL
user_story.benefit: git clients are routed to the right local clone and enumeration of workspaces is prevented

acceptance_criteria.action: look up the workspace by `workspace-slug` in the database, verify the workspace's `org_id` matches the organization identified by `org-slug`, verify `clone_status` equals `ready`, then open the repository at `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<slug>/trunk/` via `PlainOpen` and return its `storer.Storer` to the go-git server transport
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: on success, the repository storer is passed to the transport session; no HTTP response is produced at this stage
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a git request arrives with `:org` and `:slug` path parameters

acceptance_criteria.action: return `transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound` from the `server.Loader`, causing the handler to respond with a not-found error
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: no workspace with the given `workspace-slug` exists in the database

acceptance_criteria.action: return `transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound` to prevent workspace enumeration
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the workspace's `org_id` does not match the organization identified by `org-slug`

acceptance_criteria.action: return `transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound` from the `server.Loader`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body indicating the workspace is not servable

edge_cases.action: log the error and return an internal server error response
edge_cases.error_condition: `PlainOpen` fails due to a filesystem error (missing directory, permission denied, corrupted repository)

edge_cases.action: return HTTP 404 to prevent enumeration of workspaces the requester does not own
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the authenticated user is not the workspace owner and is not an admin

edge_cases.action: return an internal server error and not expose database error details to the client
edge_cases.error_condition: the database query for the workspace times out or returns an unexpected error

user_story.benefit: only authorized users and agents can read or write workspace repositories

acceptance_criteria.action: permit both fetch/clone and push operations on any workspace
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: passes the request to the next handler
acceptance_criteria.state: the resolved identity is an admin token

acceptance_criteria.action: permit the fetch/clone operation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: passes the request to the next handler
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a fetch or clone request arrives
acceptance_criteria.condition: the resolved identity is the workspace owner's API key

acceptance_criteria.action: permit the push operation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: passes the request to the next handler
acceptance_criteria.condition: the resolved identity is the workspace owner's API key

acceptance_criteria.action: permit the fetch/clone operation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: passes the request to the next handler
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a fetch or clone request arrives
acceptance_criteria.condition: the resolved identity is a PAT with `git:read` or `git:write` scope belonging to the workspace owner

acceptance_criteria.action: permit the push operation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: passes the request to the next handler
acceptance_criteria.condition: the resolved identity is a PAT with `git:write` scope belonging to the workspace owner

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the push
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a push request arrives from a PAT with only `git:read` scope

edge_cases.action: return HTTP 404 to prevent enumeration
edge_cases.error_condition: a valid PAT with `git:read` or `git:write` scope belongs to a user who is not the workspace owner and is not an admin

edge_cases.action: return HTTP 404 to prevent enumeration
edge_cases.error_condition: a valid API key belongs to a user who is not the workspace owner and is not an admin

user_story.goal: persist the new HEAD commit SHA to the database after a push completes
user_story.benefit: the hub database reflects the current state of the workspace's local clone

acceptance_criteria.action: read the new HEAD commit SHA from the repository and update the `head_sha` column on the workspace database row
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the database row's `head_sha` reflects the SHA of the new HEAD commit; the HTTP response to the git client is unaffected
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a `ReceivePackSession` completes successfully (the client's pack has been written to the local clone)

acceptance_criteria.action: not propagate the pushed commits to the upstream remote; the local clone at `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<slug>/trunk/` diverges from upstream until the next archive operation

edge_cases.action: log the error but do not fail the git push response; the push is already committed to the local clone
edge_cases.return_contract: the git client receives a successful push response; the `head_sha` database update failure is logged as an error
edge_cases.error_condition: the database update of `head_sha` fails after the pack has been written to disk

edge_cases.action: log the error and skip the `head_sha` update without failing the push response
edge_cases.return_contract: the git client receives a successful push response; the error is logged
edge_cases.error_condition: reading the new HEAD SHA from the repository after the push fails (e.g., detached HEAD or empty repository edge case)

edge_cases.action: not update `head_sha` and return an error to the git client via the pkt-line protocol
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a pkt-line error body (per git smart HTTP protocol); `head_sha` is unchanged
edge_cases.error_condition: the `ReceivePackSession` itself fails (pack data is corrupt or the session errors out)

edge_cases.action: serialize writes via the go-git repository storer's locking semantics; the second push either succeeds after the first or fails with a conflict error returned to the client
edge_cases.return_contract: at most one push succeeds atomically; the other receives a pkt-line error response
edge_cases.error_condition: two concurrent push requests arrive for the same workspace

user_story.goal: resolve a transport.Endpoint to a repository storer for the requested workspace
user_story.benefit: the go-git transport layer can serve the correct repository without knowing hub's workspace model

acceptance_criteria.action: extract the `workspace-slug` from the endpoint path, look up the workspace in the database, verify `clone_status` is `ready`, open the repository via `PlainOpen` at `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<slug>/trunk/`, and return the repository's `storer.Storer`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns `(storer.Storer, nil)` on success
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the go-git transport calls `Load(ep transport.Endpoint)` on the custom loader

acceptance_criteria.action: return `transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound` so the go-git transport produces a standard not-found error
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns `(nil, transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound)`
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the workspace is not found, not ready, or the org check fails

edge_cases.action: return the underlying error wrapped with context rather than `transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound`, so the HTTP handler can distinguish a 500 from a 404
edge_cases.error_condition: `PlainOpen` returns an error other than repository-not-found (e.g., I/O error)

edge_cases.action: return `transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound`
edge_cases.error_condition: the endpoint path does not contain a recognizable `workspace-slug` segment

user_story.goal: bridge HTTP request/response bodies to go-git upload-pack and receive-pack sessions
user_story.benefit: standard git clients can communicate with the hub git server using the smart HTTP protocol without modification

acceptance_criteria.action: create an `UploadPackSession` or `ReceivePackSession` from `server.NewServer(loader)`, call `AdvertisedReferences()` on the session, encode the result as a pkt-line ref advertisement with the appropriate capability flush, and write it to the HTTP response
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the correct Content-Type and a well-formed pkt-line ref advertisement body

acceptance_criteria.action: stream the HTTP request body as input to the session and stream the session output back as the HTTP response body, flushing as data becomes available
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the correct Content-Type and a streaming pack response body
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a valid POST request arrives at `git-upload-pack` or `git-receive-pack`

acceptance_criteria.action: encode the error message in pkt-line error format and write it to the response body if headers have not yet been sent; if headers were already sent, close the connection
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a pkt-line `ERR <message>` body if headers were not yet sent, or closes the connection abruptly if streaming was already in progress
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the go-git session returns an error during streaming

edge_cases.action: detect the closed connection, abort the session, and release all resources (session, open file handles) without leaving partial state
edge_cases.return_contract: no response is sent; resources are cleaned up and the error is logged
edge_cases.error_condition: the git client disconnects mid-stream during a push or fetch

edge_cases.action: apply a request-scoped context deadline so the session is cancelled and the connection is closed after the timeout elapses
edge_cases.return_contract: the HTTP connection is closed; the session context is cancelled; resources are released
edge_cases.error_condition: the go-git session hangs and does not return within a reasonable time

edge_cases.action: the go-git session returns an error which is encoded as a pkt-line error response
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a pkt-line `ERR <message>` body
edge_cases.error_condition: the request body for a POST pack operation is empty or truncated

correctness_properties.title: Only ready workspaces are served
correctness_properties.invariant: all four git endpoints return HTTP 404 and never open the repository filesystem

correctness_properties.title: Unauthenticated requests always receive a 401 challenge
correctness_properties.invariant: the response is HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="af-hub"` and the repository is never accessed

correctness_properties.title: Anti-enumeration: non-owner access returns 404 not 403
correctness_properties.for_any: authenticated request where the credential owner is not the workspace owner and is not an admin
correctness_properties.invariant: the response is HTTP 404 regardless of whether the workspace exists

correctness_properties.title: git:write implies read access
correctness_properties.for_any: PAT with `git:write` scope and no explicit `git:read` scope
correctness_properties.invariant: both fetch/clone and push operations are permitted on workspaces the PAT owner owns

correctness_properties.title: head_sha is updated after every successful push
correctness_properties.invariant: the `head_sha` column in the database equals the SHA of the HEAD commit in the local clone at `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<slug>/trunk/`

correctness_properties.title: Org slug mismatch always returns 404
correctness_properties.for_any: request where the `org-slug` in the URL does not match the `org_id` of the workspace identified by `workspace-slug`
correctness_properties.invariant: the response is HTTP 404 regardless of whether the workspace exists under a different org

correctness_properties.title: Response Content-Type matches the git smart HTTP specification
correctness_properties.for_any: successful response from any of the four git endpoints
correctness_properties.invariant: the Content-Type header exactly matches the git smart HTTP specification for that endpoint (upload-pack advertisement, receive-pack advertisement, upload-pack result, or receive-pack result)

steps.action: runs `git clone http://x-token-auth:<af_pat_...>@<hub-host>:<port>/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git`
receives GET `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` and routes it to the git info/refs handler after applying the auth middleware
extracts the `af_pat_...` credential from the Basic auth password field, resolves it to a PAT identity with `git:read` scope via apikit, and attaches the identity to the request context
verifies the PAT owner matches the workspace owner and the PAT has `git:read` scope; permits the request
extracts `org-slug` and `workspace-slug` from the path, queries the database to find the workspace, verifies `org_id` matches the org, verifies `clone_status` is `ready`
calls `PlainOpen` on `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<workspace-slug>/trunk/` and returns the `storer.Storer` to the go-git transport

creates an `UploadPackSession`, calls `AdvertisedReferences()`, encodes the result as a pkt-line ref advertisement, and writes it to the HTTP response with Content-Type `application/x-git-upload-pack-advertisement`
receives the ref advertisement, then sends a POST to `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/git-upload-pack` with the pack negotiation request
streams the POST body into the `UploadPackSession` and streams the pack data response back to the client with Content-Type `application/x-git-upload-pack-result`
receives the complete pack and the local clone is created on disk

execution_paths.title: git push happy path with head_sha update

steps.action: runs `git push` from a local clone of the workspace repository
receives GET `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack` and routes it to the git info/refs handler
resolves the credential to a PAT identity with `git:write` scope
verifies the PAT owner matches the workspace owner and the PAT has `git:write` scope; permits the request
creates a `ReceivePackSession`, advertises refs, and returns the ref advertisement to the client
sends a POST to `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/git-receive-pack` with the pack data
streams the pack data into the `ReceivePackSession`; the session writes the new objects and updates refs in the local clone at `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>/<workspace-slug>/trunk/`
reads the new HEAD commit SHA from the repository and updates the `head_sha` column on the workspace database row
streams the receive-pack result back to the client with Content-Type `application/x-git-receive-pack-result`
receives a successful push confirmation; the local hub clone and database `head_sha` reflect the new commits

execution_paths.title: Unauthenticated git request rejected with Basic auth challenge

steps.action: runs `git clone http://<hub-host>:<port>/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git` without credentials
receives GET `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` with no `Authorization` header
detects the missing `Authorization` header and returns HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="af-hub"`
prompts the user for credentials or fails if running non-interactively
runs `git push` using a PAT that has only `git:read` scope
receives GET `/git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`
resolves the credential to a PAT identity with only `git:read` scope
detects that the PAT lacks `git:write` scope for a receive-pack operation and rejects the request
returns HTTP 403 to the git client
reports a permission error to the user; no data is transferred

error_handling.condition: No `Authorization` header present on a git request
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="af-hub"` header and no body

error_handling.condition: Invalid or unrecognized credential in the Basic auth password field
Valid credentials but the authenticated user does not own the workspace and is not an admin
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 404 to prevent workspace enumeration

error_handling.condition: Workspace not found in the database
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body

error_handling.condition: `org-slug` in the URL does not match the workspace's `org_id`
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body (anti-enumeration)
Return HTTP 404 with a pkt-line error body indicating the workspace is not servable

error_handling.condition: Push attempted by a PAT with only `git:read` scope
Invalid or unsupported `service` query parameter on `info/refs`
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 403 with a pkt-line error body per the git smart HTTP specification

error_handling.condition: `PlainOpen` fails due to a filesystem error when opening the repository
error_handling.behavior: Log the error and return HTTP 500

error_handling.condition: go-git session error during streaming (corrupt pack, protocol error)
error_handling.behavior: Encode the error in pkt-line `ERR <message>` format and write to the response body if headers have not been sent; otherwise close the connection
Abort the session, release all resources (session, file handles), and log the disconnection without leaving partial state

error_handling.condition: Database update of `head_sha` fails after a successful push
error_handling.behavior: Log the error but return a successful push response to the git client; the push is already committed to the local clone

symbols.name: PlainOpen
symbols.notes: Opens an existing git repository at the given path. Returns an error if the path does not contain a valid git repository.

symbols.name: NewServer
symbols.notes: Creates a go-git server transport that uses the provided Loader to resolve repository endpoints.

symbols.name: Loader
symbols.notes: Interface that the custom hub loader must implement to resolve workspace slugs to repository storers.

symbols.name: ErrRepositoryNotFound
symbols.notes: Sentinel error returned by a Loader when the requested repository cannot be found. The server transport maps this to a git protocol not-found error.
